messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGER: High tail latency for hosted model redwood-gen-large (us-west-2). Paging @eng-oncall. Severity: P2. Links: https://dash.redwood.example/incident/1723456789

Alex Chen: I'm on it. Seeing 95th latency ~12s for gen-large. Query rate up ~2x in last 10m. Any customer tickets?

Maria Gomez: yes, support ticket #4321 from Acme corp reporting timeouts. Pulling logs now. I'll paste the hot slices.

Taylor Reed: Noticed queue depth spike on runtime-queue: capacity metric 'ready_replicas' lagging HPA. Suspect warmup lag after autoscale. 

Priya Singh: Oncall handoff note: if we escalate, we can route traffic to gen-medium fallback (slightly lower quality) to reduce token time.

Alex Chen: Diagnostics: 
- kubectl get hpa -n runtime
```sh
NAME             REFERENCE                TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
inference-hpa    Deployment/inference     80%/100%  2         20        2
```
- kubectl describe deployment inference | grep -i 'update' -A3
(see events: 'scaled up' but pods stuck in ContainerCreating)

Maria Gomez: Logs from runtime controller:
```
2026-03-10T15:12:03Z WARN warmup: cold-kv-cache miss for model redwood-gen-large, initiating warmup (gpu 0)
2026-03-10T15:12:05Z ERROR pool: no available ready GPUs, enqueue request, current_pool=full, queue_depth=548
```

Taylor Reed: Prometheus shot: gpu_utilization at 98% on pool us-west-2-gpu-a, OOM evictions none. Node autoscaler pending nodes not ready due to image pull slowdown (registry throttling).

Alex Chen: Hypothesis list (putting here so we can iterate):
1) HPA metric warmup lag — metrics delayed, so HPA didn't scale early.
2) Nodepool provisioning delay (registry/image pull) -> pods stuck in ContainerCreating.
3) Runtime warmup cold cache -> first requests block while KV warmup occurs -> queue buildup -> autoscaler sees short bursts and can't react.
4) Model variant pins causing routing to saturated pool.

Maria Gomez: Action items I'm taking now: collect `kubectl describe nodes` and the full controller logs -> uploading to gist
Link: https://gist.github.com/redwood-inc/abc123 (logs + extracted timeline)

Taylor Reed: I'm going to trigger an emergency manual scale of the GPU nodepool to add 4 nodes (cloud CLI) and also manually increase HPA max to 30 to allow faster autoscale. Command I'll run:
```sh
cloudctl nodepools resize us-west-2-gpu-a --add 4 --yes
kubectl patch hpa inference-hpa -n runtime -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":30}}'
```

Priya Singh: I'm going to start a warmup flood to pre-populate KV caches for gen-large on the new nodes (10 QPS for 2 minutes). Will post script.

Alex Chen: Temporal timeline so far (times are system clock):
- 15:09 UTC: request rate begins to ramp (+2x)
- 15:11 UTC: first HPA scale event triggered, but pods delayed (ContainerCreating)
- 15:12 UTC: queue depth crosses 400, latency climbs
- 15:15 UTC: oncall page
- 15:17 UTC: manual scale initiated
- 15:21 UTC: nodes start becoming Ready
- 15:24 UTC: warmup flood started
- 15:27 UTC: queue depth falls to ~40, p95 latency back to ~850ms

Maria Gomez: Customer impact note: 3 enterprises reported errors, estimated 1.2k requests failed. I've updated incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.example/incident/1723456789

Taylor Reed: Post-mitigation steps I recommend (for the RCA):
- Fix: add proactive warmup hook during scale events to reduce cold-start penalty.
- Fix: add image pull acceleration (cached images) or use faster registry endpoint.
- Observability: add synthetic warmup metric to HPA so scale decisions account for ready_warm_pods.

Alex Chen: Can someone paste `kubectl get pods -n runtime` output for snapshot at 15:13?

Maria Gomez: pasted from gist (trimmed):
```
NAME                                 READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
inference-xyz-1                      0/1     ContainerCreating  0          2m
inference-xyz-2                      0/1     ContainerCreating  0          2m
inference-xyz-3                      0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   3          8m
```

Priya Singh: Live mitigation notes: we've routed non-enterprise traffic to gen-medium via routing policy for now. That dropped overall queue pressure by ~30%.

Taylor Reed: Request: eng-runtime, can we prioritize fixing the pool eviction threshold? It looks like the pool scheduler held onto long-running sessions blocking new warmups. Feedback ticket created: #runtime-541

Alex Chen: Handoff to next oncall (night): state=stabilized, p95 back under SLO for now but we still have recovery tasks. Tasks to pick up:
- monitor nodes Ready and eviction events
- follow up on registry throttle mitigation
- RCA writeup (assign to Maria for logs, Taylor for infra).

Priya Singh: leaving detailed instructions in runbook: https://playbooks.redwood.example/warmup-on-scale

oncall-bot: Incident status updated to mitigated (P2 -> monitoring). Next update scheduled in 2h.

Alex Chen: Final note for RCA thread: please add any remaining evidence (traces, request IDs) here. I'll draft timeline and hypothesis resolution. :thumbsup:
